rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says أَعْلَمُ can mean عالم: God has no equal knower; alternatively it is truly comparative against any hypothetical other knower.
rows.anchor: أعلم } بمعنى عالم بالمهتدي والضال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: علم may take its object directly or with ب; direct attachment can reflect stronger knowledge, a more evident object, required certainty, or greater force of the action.
rows.anchor: علمته وعلمت به مستعملان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here أعلم is a noun denoting an action, whose weaker verbal government accounts for the preposition ب before its object.
rows.anchor: كما كان المستعمل اسما دالا على فعل ضعف عمله لتعلقه بالمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across these passages, mentioning the astray before the guided threatens the stubborn opponents and consoles the Prophet, since he faces them in each context.
rows.anchor: فذكرهم أولا تهديدا لهم وتسلية لقلب نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eternal divine knowledge relates to an event as it actually occurs, without a delay between occurrence and knowledge; no atom escapes God in heaven or earth.
rows.anchor: فهو أن العلم القديم يتعلق بالمعلوم على ما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active participle governs like a verb for a future sense, but not for a past one; hence one says أنا غدا ضارب زيدا, while a past construction requires a finite verb or genitive attachment.
rows.anchor: اسم الفاعل يعمل عمل الفعل إذا كان بمعنى المستقبل ولا يعمل عمله إذا كان ماضيا

rows.speaker: النحاة
rows.claim: Grammarians explain أعلم من يضل in 6:117 as يعلم من يضل, since the elative is formed from an intransitive verb and a transitive verb must be recast as intransitive.
rows.anchor: قالت النحاة في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers the grammarians by taking أعلم in the divine attribute as truly comparative: God is knowing, with no knower like Him; this is better than reducing it to عالم alone.
rows.anchor: وأما أنا فقد أجبت عن هذا بأن قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage uses past ضل because the turning away had occurred and the Prophet had despaired and been told to withdraw; 6:117 uses يضل after the warning that most people would mislead him.
rows.anchor: ههنا حصل الضلال في الماضي وتأكد حيث حصل يأس الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمر بالإعراض

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the verse concerns al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra: after the Prophet's admonition moved him, a man dissuaded him, promised to bear his sins for payment, and he gave part before turning away.
rows.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : نزلت الآية في الوليد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say it concerned ʿUthmān, who stopped almsgiving after his maternal half-brother ʿAbd Allāh b. Saʿd offered to bear his sins; Rāzī rejects this as unestablished and contrary to ʿUthmān's character.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : نزلت في عثمان رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī treats the referent broadly as anyone turning away from the reminder out of self-sufficiency, a type already mentioned in 53:29; such a person seeks other pursuits instead of attending its reminder.
rows.anchor: وكان التولي من جملة أنواعه تولى المستغني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed فاء follows the prior account of God's knowledge, power, and recompense: since people need the Prophet's teaching and following to avoid major sins, turning away follows a state of extreme need.
rows.anchor: هو ما تقدم من بيان علم الله وقدرته

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take الذي as a particular known man, namely al-Walīd; Rāzī instead reads it as the previously mentioned general class of those who turned away.
rows.anchor: على ما قال بعض المفسرين عائد إلى معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although من is general, Arabic commonly resumes it according to its singular wording, as in 28:84, من جاء بالحسنة فله, rather than according to its plural sense.
rows.anchor: العود إلى اللفظ كثير شائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preceding al-Walīd account, the little he gave was the amount he had promised, and أكدى means he withheld the rest instead of giving it all.
rows.anchor: على ما تقدم هو المقدار الذي أعطاه الوليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that stopping was blameless because the gift was not owed misses the point: offering money cannot transfer another's sins, and a noble Arab customarily keeps a promise once made.
rows.anchor: نقول فيه بيان خروجهم عن العقل والعرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī's broader reading is that the man turned from revelation while seeking only worldly life, giving little toward what was due to secure the affairs of the afterlife and then stopping.
rows.anchor: تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about unseen knowledge answers 53:30: the man's limited worldly knowledge is no knowledge of the unseen or of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي لم يعلم الغيب وما في الآخرة

words: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِى صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scrolls passage and the statement that one burdened soul bears no other's burden correspond to 53:30–31, since both passages explain recompense.
rows.anchor: لأن الكلامين جميعا لبيان الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī proposes a shift from idolaters to scriptured people: a person with a book gave God's rights for a short time, then stopped when Muhammad came; the scrolls already taught individual accountability, so the man may be from the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يقال : إن الله تعالى لما بين حال المشركين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One proposed sense of أكدى is that a digger reached hard ground or bedrock where digging became difficult or stopped.
rows.anchor: قيل هو من بلغ الكدية وهي الأرض الصلبة لا تحفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers the sense of turning back or withholding: أكديته means that I repelled or stopped him.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أنه الرد والمنع يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question exposes the turner's ignorance and need, and the ugliness of turning away when he ought to heed; unseen knowledge is knowledge of what is hidden from creatures.
rows.anchor: المراد جهل المتولي وحاجته وبيان قبح التولي مع الحاجة إلى الإقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing would excuse turning away only when the unseen is directly visible, at the time faith no longer benefits; until then a person needs the guide who leads toward a destination not yet seen.
rows.anchor: تتمة بيان وقت جواز التولي وهو حصول الرؤية وهو الوقت الذي لا ينفع الإيمان فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible object of يرى is the belief that one person's burden is carried by another: the man supposes this while unaware that each bears only his own.
rows.anchor: هو احتمال الواحد وزر الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, يرى has no expressed object and means that the man sees his own judgment as sufficient, needing neither guide nor warner.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن لا يكون له مفعول تقديره فهو يرى رأي نظر غير محتاج إلى هاد ونذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse tests the alternative excuse of complete ignorance: someone who fully knows needs no teaching, while one wholly unaware, like a sleeper, is not addressed; neither condition applies, so the turner is not excused.
rows.anchor: فقال : هذا المتولي هل علم الكل فجاز له التولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, the phrase means the teachings found in Moses' scrolls—such as monotheism and resurrection—so the Prophet's message of that content addresses both idolaters and People of the Book.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد ما فيها لا بصفة كونه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, بما means the very contents as they stand in those scrolls, making the address specifically to the People of the Book who received those scriptures.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بما في الصحف مع كونه فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural صحف most likely reflects numerous scrolls, not merely attribution to Moses and Abraham as dual possessors; the many tablets each count as a scroll.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنها كثيرة ، قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent content is the rule that no bearer carries another's burden, though the phrase may cover more because the scrolls contain more than this alone.
rows.anchor: هو ما ذكر بقوله : { ألا تزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second proposed content is that the afterlife is better than worldly life, as stated about the first scriptures in 87:18–19.
rows.anchor: هو أن الآخرة خير من الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view is that all foundational doctrines occur in every scripture; the command to follow earlier guidance concerns religious fundamentals, not legal branches that differ between communities.
rows.anchor: أصول الدين كلها مذكورة في الكتب بأسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī first says eloquent speech needs no special rationale for naming Moses before Abraham; either order is valid.
rows.anchor: مثل هذا في كلام الفصحاء لا يطلب له فائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As possible rationales, the earlier sūra orders the names by the scriptures' order of descent, whereas this passage addresses Jews first or names Moses first because his scrolls were numerous and familiar; Abraham's were less known.
rows.anchor: وأما ههنا فقد قلنا إن الكلام مع أهل الكتاب وهم اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says Moses is often mentioned later because the Prophet dealt largely with polytheists and Jews, while polytheists honored Abraham as their forefather.
rows.anchor: كثيرا ما ذكر الله موسى فأخر ذكره عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of وفّى is fulfilling covenants, with the doubled form intensifying the sense; Abraham fulfilled his vow and submitted his son to sacrifice, as the dream was confirmed.
rows.anchor: أنه الوفاء الذي يذكر في العهود وعلى هذا فالتشديد للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading derives وفّى from completing: Abraham completed God's trials, as in the verse saying he completed the words with which his Lord tested him.
rows.anchor: أنه من التوفية التي من الوفاء وهو التمام والتوفية الإتمام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation says Abraham rendered God's bodily rights, directly contrasting him with the person who gave little and stopped.
rows.anchor: أي أعطى حقوق الله في بدنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī explains Abraham's fulfillment by saying he kept his promise to seek forgiveness for his father and did so; God's refusal taught that each person receives only the fruits of his own effort and no soul bears another's sin.
rows.anchor: فاستغفر ووفى بالعهد ولم يغفر الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was praised as وفّى because Jews, polytheists, and Muslims all accepted this description, whereas polytheists might hesitate to praise Moses.
rows.anchor: فلأنه كان متفقا عليه بين اليهود والمشركين والمسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī takes ألا تزر as an appositive explaining بما: the scrolls' content is that no burdened soul bears another's burden; he recalls the alternatives that it may point to the better afterlife or foundational doctrines.
rows.anchor: هو ما بينه بقوله { ألا تزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here أن is the light form of heavy أن; lightening is obligatory before a following verb or a particle governing a verb, since a verb cannot itself govern another verb directly.
rows.anchor: أن خفيفة من الثقيلة كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وازرة means a soul expected to carry a burden, not one already loaded; thus the verse meaningfully denies that even a potential bearer takes on another's burden.
rows.anchor: المراد من الوازرة هي التي يتوقع منها الوزر والحمل لا التي وزرت وحملت

words: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This completes the account of accountability: just as another cannot carry one's sin, another's good deed does not benefit one who did no good and cannot supply him a reward.
rows.anchor: أن سيئته لا يتحملها عنه أحد بين له أن حسنة الغير لا تجدي نفعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī holds الإنسان to be general, despite objections that relatives' charity, fasting, and prayer benefit the dead and that tenfold reward exceeds the deed.
rows.anchor: أنه عام وهو الحق وقيل عليه بأن في الأخبار أن ما يأتي به القريب من الصدقة والصوم يصل إلى الميت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An objection cites unspecified reports that a close relative's charity and fasting reach the dead, and says prayer also benefits them; no report authority is named here.
rows.anchor: في الأخبار أن ما يأتي به القريب من الصدقة والصوم يصل إلى الميت والدعاء أيضا نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī answers that the deceased receives a relative's charity only through his own effort of faith; the tenfold increase is also within what one seeks by doing good in hope of God's promised generosity.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان إن لم يسع في أن يكون له صدقة القريب بالإيمان لا يكون له صدقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though سعى usually means performed work, not merely seeking a thing (which would take فيه), the verse refers to the work's reward or to the deed preserved for its agent, not necessarily the deed itself.
rows.anchor: لا بد من زيادة فإن قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that الإنسان here means only the unbeliever is weak.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من الإنسان الكافر دون المؤمن وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the claim that this rule belonged to an earlier law and was abrogated in Muhammad's law, where people supposedly receive what they did not earn; he says the proposed abrogation is needless.
rows.anchor: وهو باطل إذ لا حاجة إلى هذا التكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the literal reading, a person's work remains محفوظ with God without loss and is then requited, as 99:7 says that whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
rows.anchor: له عين ما سعى محفوظ عند الله تعالى ولا نقصان يدخله ثم يجزى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in 53:39 is more plausibly a verbal noun, supported by 53:40, وأن سعيه سوف يرى: the verbal noun can denote the object worked upon, as خلق الله means God's created thing.
rows.anchor: كونها مصدرية أظهر بدليل

rows.speaker: المشهور
rows.claim: The well-known reading includes every deed: good deeds are rewarded and evil deeds punished.
rows.anchor: المشهور أنهما لكل عمل فالخير مثاب عليه والشر معاقب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says the apparent point is benefits from good deeds: لام marks what is for a person, unlike على for what is against him; full recompense fits good, while evil may be matched, lessened, or forgiven.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لبيان الخيرات يدل عليه اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense سعى encourages good works: future promises to pray or give are not yet earned or recorded, so the verse says a person has only what he has already done.
rows.anchor: الماضي دون المستقبل لزياد الحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سوف يرى means that a person's effort will be shown and disclosed: believers rejoice in seeing their good deeds, perhaps before all creatures, while the sight brings the unbeliever grief; the phrase may also mean God will see it, as in 9:105.
rows.anchor: أي يعرض عليه ويكشف له من أريته الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says a past deed is shown in a beautiful form if it was righteous.
rows.anchor: يراه على صورة جميلة إن كان العمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Rāzī's theological position, it is plausible for a past deed to be seen after its occurrence because every existent can be seen and God can restore what has ceased to exist.
rows.anchor: هو على مذهبنا غير بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A figurative reading takes seeing one's kindness before a king to mean seeing its reward; Rāzī calls this remote because the next verse separately says the person will be fully requited.
rows.anchor: وهو أن ذلك مجاز عن الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes the pronoun refer to سعي: the person is rewarded for his effort; جزى can take two objects or three with a preposition, and the preposition may be omitted with the verb attached directly.
rows.anchor: الهاء ضمير السعي أي ثم يجزى الإنسان سعيه بالجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to الجزاء: the person is given a reward, with الجزاء الأوفى explaining or appositive to an understood جزاء, as in 21:3.
rows.anchor: وفيه وجه آخر وهو أن الضمير للجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fullest recompense suits righteous believers, prompting the objection that Hell is also called a plentiful recompense; Rāzī answers that Hell is fuller in harm than the benefit of sins, so it is complete from that perspective.
rows.anchor: الجزاء الأوفى على ما ذكرنا يليق بالمؤمنين الصالحين
